prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Edit target: image 1, the existing OS-Atlas project cover. Identity reference: image 2, the user's original OS-Atlas robot logo.
User revision: differentiate this cover strongly in color, setting and robot details. Preserve GUI grounding and the recognizable robot identity while replacing the entire night-time blue-and-gold library with a bright daylight interface-cartography studio.
New scene: a precise navigation robot at a daylight-lit drafting and GUI-mapping workbench. Warm ivory ceramic work surfaces, sand-colored paper-like mapping sheets, clear glass interface plates, small brushed-brass hinges and calibration tools, and crisp cobalt-blue geometric control panels. A broad rectangular window provides soft natural sunlight; background architecture is plain, airy and modern. One physical slanted drafting board in the foreground carries a fine unlabeled coordinate grid. One nearby upright pale-glass GUI panel contains generous geometric application blocks; the robot points at exactly one clearly highlighted cobalt-blue button with a thin warm amber border. A tiny precise point at the fingertip and a single short fine guide line connect the action to the target. The coordinate grid must be geometric and unlabeled, with no numbers. This is a deliberate interface-navigation and grounding workspace, not a wall of giant screens.
Mascot identity: keep the warm-ivory rounded face, black circular eyes with white highlights, friendly curved smile, curved eyebrows, swept dark head detail, and distinctive round black headset from image 2. Preserve the four-dot chest panel and blue circular badge with an abstract white upward chevron, without text. Evolve the body into a refined navigation robot: matte ivory ceramic armor, small brass fasteners, black precision joints, cobalt cuff or shoulder accents, and slim articulated fingers. Keep the ivory face instead of a dark digital face screen. Do not borrow the blue-eyed gold robots from other projects.
Palette: mostly warm ivory-white and sand gold under daylight, with cobalt-blue accents. Restrained brass detail, very little cyan. The whole scene should appear lighter and warmer than the old cover, with clear material color separation. No starry midnight-blue atmosphere, navy-and-gold library palette, or luminous teal wall-of-screens.
Style: high-quality painterly illustration with tangible materials and depth: slightly textured ceramic, delicate brass machining, fibrous matte paper, clear layered glass, soft sunlit reflections, nuanced cast shadows, and modest surface wear. A refined illustrated research cover, not a flat vector diagram, emoji, sticker, or plastic logo cutout.
Composition: square 1:1, fully opaque background. Three-quarter view with the prominent robot on the left/middle, its clear pointing gesture reaching one target button on the right, and a geometric map board in the foreground. Maintain a readable silhouette and a distinct cobalt background accent behind the ivory head. Keep the entire head and pointing hand inside the frame. The central subject and target should read in a 120-pixel thumbnail. Major recomposition of image 1 is intended.
Constraints: no text, letters, digits, logos, labels, watermarks, trademarks or chart tick labels. No Gothic arches, arched windows, library shelves, star fields, ornamental golden walls, night lighting, dense targeting crosshairs, extra robots, or screens stacked everywhere.
